newsitem.title: ITALY: Milan shares chase bonds higher on budget optimism.
newsitem.headline: Milan shares chase bonds higher on budget optimism.

text.p: Italian shares closed sharply higher on Friday following domestic bonds upwards on optimism over the accord struck on Italy's 1997 budget which is aimed at putting Italy on track to join a European single currency.
Shares were very much in catch up mode throughout most of Friday following surging bonds and the rampant lira which hit new 25-months highs in late Thursday trade.
"The deal on the budget has brightened prospects and encouraged investors into Italian stocks," said one dealer.
The all-share Mibtel index ended up 3.09 percent at 10,154 and the Mib30 index was 3.48 percent higher at 15,323.

Dealers said news that the government was ready to unveil a 1997 financial budget to cut Italy's deficit by 62.5 trillion lire rather that the 32.4 trillion lire originally planned was greeted positively by financial markets.
"The markets have swallowed the belief that the government is firm on financial discipline and determined to join the single European currency," said one share trader.

Among the leaders in the blue-chips was Pirelli up 3.15 percent at 2,750 lire after strong first-half 1996 results late Thursday, while others also moved up with ENI 3.54 percent higher at 7,691 lire and Montedison up 4.77 percent at 985.5.
Telecoms stocks were firmer with Telecom Italia, STET and TIM all rising strongly as dealers saw the financial budget encouraging international investors into buying of these stocks.
Telecom Italia ended up 3.88 percent at 3,397 lire, STET 4.52 percent higher at 5,299 lire and mobile phone group TIM 4.97 percent firmer at 3,382 lire.
